newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says to list 1.5 mln JR Tokai shares Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: Japan says to list 1.5 mln JR Tokai shares Oct 8.

text.p: Japan's Transport Ministry announced on Tuesday that it will list 1.5 million state-owned shares of Central Japan Railway Co (JR Tokai) on October 8.
"In order to smoothly carry out sales and listing of the shares as planned, we want to do our best to prepare for it," Transport Minister Makoto Koga said in a statement.

Of the total 1.5 million shares to be listed on Japanese bourses, 700,000 shares will be auctioned and the rest will be sold in the market through a secondary offering. At present, JR Tokai's existing shares total 2.24 million.
On June 30, JR Tokai formally applied for its shares to be listed on the Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya and Kyoto bourses.

JR Tokai, one of six private railway operators formed on the breakup of the former state-run Japanese national Railways (JNR), which was burdened by a mounting deficit, will be the third JR firm to be listed on Japan's stock exchanges.
Shares of East Japan Railway Co (JR East) and West Japan Railway Co (JR West) are already being traded on Japanese bourses.

JNR Settlement Corp, the government agent in charge of selling state-owned shares and land left over by debt-ridden JNR, said on Tuesday that applications for the auction and the secondary offering should be made between August 4 and August 7.
Winners of the auction will be decided on August 21 and the payment date is September 17.
The price for the secondary offering of shares will be decided on August 25, after taking into account the results of the auctions.
The payment for the secondary offering should be made between September 18 and September 26, and the shares will be actually transferred on October 8, it said.
Snowballing national debt left from the former JNR has posed a big headache for the Japanese government, which is currently struggling to improve its severe fiscal conditions, analysts said.

Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Saturday that the Japanese people will have to foot the bill for 23 trillion yen in debt still left from the privatisation of JNR 10 years ago, which was equivalent to 200,000 yen per citizen.

He said that of the 28 trillion yen in debt still left, five trillion will be covered by selling off Japan Railways' real estate and stock holdings. The remaining 23 trillion will have to come from either the government's existing funds or from establishing a new tax, he said.

The planned listing of JR Tokai shares, on the other hand, is likely to spur worries about a supply glut in the stock market, as it will probably pave the way for sales of other state-owned shares in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp as well as JR East, analysts said.
